correctness.rationale: RESULT.md defines zero-based Fibonacci and inflated Lucas words, fixes the irrational gamma and the aligned indicator event, and proves the relevant Beatty floor-difference test. The kth Fibonacci 1 occurs at floor(k phi^2)-1; inflating every 1 twice puts the Lucas 1s at floor(k(phi+2))-2,-1. Replacing reciprocal slopes by gamma yields both simultaneous rotation cutoffs. The f=1 region consists of five explicit intervals, precisely three within the Lucas-one interval. Computing four lengths gives the table, equality density and covariance; they sum to 1 and are positive. The convergent-denominator grid argument and bounded CF coefficients of gamma prove O(log N) discrepancy for finite interval unions; finite blocks are intersections of shifted intervals with endpoints in Q(sqrt5). The exact-integer standalone verifier recomputes the first 50,000 symbols from separate definitions and independently checks high-precision coding and counts. Finite tests are not asserted to prove the unbounded result.
